cards.title: Are splay trees dynamically optimal?
cards.formal: Fix n ordered keys and an access sequence X. In the root-BST model, an access is served by rotations until its key is at the root; its cost is one plus the number of rotations. Let OPT(X) minimize total cost over offline executions, allowing an optimal initial tree. Is there a universal constant C such that, for every initial splay tree T₀ and every X, $\mathrm{cost}_{\mathrm{splay}}(X;T_0)\le C(\mathrm{OPT}(X)+n)$? The additive term allows an arbitrary initial configuration.
cards.definitions: Keys are [n]={1,…,n}, n≥1, ordered by their integer values. A binary search tree has one node per key, every key in a left subtree smaller than its root and every key in a right subtree larger. A rotation on a parent-child edge exchanges those two nodes while reattaching the intermediate subtree so that the order is preserved. To splay a requested key x, repeatedly apply the following bottom-up rule until x is root. If its parent is root, rotate the edge from x to its parent (zig). Otherwise let p be its parent and g its grandparent. If x and p are both left children or both right children, first rotate p above g and then x above p (zig-zig). Otherwise rotate x above p and then x above g (zig-zag). Each access costs one plus its number of rotations. The tree after the access is the initial tree for the next access. For a finite sequence X∈[n]*, cost_splay(X;T₀) is the sum of these costs starting from T₀. A comparator execution may start with any tree, knows X in full, and serves each request by any finite sequence of parent-child rotations anywhere in the current tree whose final root is the requested key. Its cost is the same one-plus-rotations sum. OPT(X) is the minimum cost over all such initial trees and executions; it is zero for the empty sequence. There are no insertions, deletions or additional node operations. This root-BST cost convention is the one used in the saved source, with the additive n term accounting for the initial tree.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove that one finite constant C bounds cost_splay(X;T₀)/(OPT(X)+n) for all n, all initial trees T₀ and all finite access sequences X, or prove that this ratio is unbounded over those inputs. A counterexample to a particular proposed value of C alone does not refute the universal-constant claim.

cards.title: Expected linear-time integer sorting for every word length
cards.formal: Does there exist a uniform Las Vegas word-RAM algorithm and a constant C such that, for every n≥2, every integer word length w≥⌈log₂(n+1)⌉, and every list x₁,…,xₙ∈{0,…,2ʷ−1}, the algorithm outputs the list in nondecreasing order with expected running time at most Cn?
cards.definitions: The input occupies n words, with one unsigned w-bit key per word; repeated keys are allowed. The output must contain exactly the input multiset in nondecreasing numerical order, with no stability requirement. The machine is sequential and has w-bit data registers and random-access memory. Unit-cost operations are reads and writes, comparisons, branches, addition and subtraction modulo 2ʷ, multiplication of two words with the product returned in two words, quotient and remainder of two words with a nonzero divisor, bitwise Boolean operations, and left or right shifts by a word-specified amount. Shifted-out bits are discarded, and shifts by at least w return zero. Addresses may use a constant number of words to index polynomially many memory cells; all address computation is charged. An operation can generate one fresh independent uniform w-bit random word. These are the only primitive operations; arbitrary-length arithmetic, a built-in sorting operation and free tables are unavailable. All preprocessing, memory initialization performed by the algorithm, and output writes count. A fixed finite program receives n and w; it may select methods according to their values but has no advice depending on them. Las Vegas means every terminating computation is correct and the algorithm terminates with probability one. Expectation is over the internal random choices for each fixed input. C must be independent of both n and w, including when w grows with n.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the existence of a single uniform, always-correct Las Vegas program whose expected running time is at most Cn on every admissible (n,w,input), for one C independent of n and w. A negative answer must show that every such sorting program has unbounded expected-time/n ratio over these inputs. A lower bound only for comparison sorting, deterministic programs, or a different word instruction set does not establish that negation.

cards.title: An explicit static problem requiring superlogarithmically many cell probes
cards.formal: Does there exist a fixed integer k≥2 and a uniformly polynomial-time computable family of Boolean functions F_n on an n-word database and a k⌈log₂ n⌉-bit query such that its optimal deterministic static cell-probe query complexity t*F(n), with word size ⌈4log₂ n⌉ bits and n⌈log₂ n⌉² memory cells, satisfies t*F(n)/log₂ n→∞ as n→∞?
cards.definitions: For each integer n≥2 put w=⌈4log₂ n⌉ and s=n⌈log₂ n⌉². A database is D∈({0,1}^w)^n, a query is q∈{0,1}^{k⌈log₂ n⌉}, and F_n(D,q)∈{0,1}. Explicit means that a single deterministic Turing machine computes F_n(D,q), given (1^n,D,q), in time polynomial in n; no advice is allowed in this definition. A data structure may preprocess D by any map E_n into s cells of w bits each. Preprocessing time is unrestricted, and this encoding may be nonlinear and nonuniform. For each query, a deterministic adaptive decision tree reads cells, choosing the next address from the query and previously read contents, and must output F_n(D,q) exactly for every database. Computation between probes is free. The trees may depend on n, F and the query, but their only access to D is through E_n(D). Each query starts without free database-dependent private information; memory is static and read-only. Define t*F(n) as the minimum, over all such encodings and trees, of the maximum number of probes over all D and q. All memory cells count toward s. This card fixes a near-linear-space, short-query, one-bit-answer specialization of the broader static lower-bound challenge; it does not assert equivalence to every space or word-size variant.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove that some fixed k and admissible uniform family F satisfy: for every real B>0 there is N such that t*F(n)>B log₂ n for every n≥N. Alternatively, prove the exact negation: for every fixed k and every admissible family F, there is a finite B>0 such that t*F(n)≤B log₂ n for arbitrarily large n. In particular, the negative answer need not establish an O(log n) bound for all sufficiently large n.

cards.title: Can a static dictionary be built deterministically in linear time?
cards.formal: Is the following proposition true? For every fixed integer d≥1 there are uniform deterministic construction and query programs A_d,Q_d and a constant C_d≥1 such that, for every n≥2, every word length ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉≤w≤d⌈log₂(n+1)⌉, and every n-record input with distinct w-bit integer keys and w-bit values, A_d builds a static dictionary in at most C_d n operations and C_d n words of total space, and Q_d answers every membership-and-value query in at most C_d operations.
cards.definitions: The universe is U_w={0,…,2ʷ−1}. An input is a list of n pairs (x_i,v_i)∈U_w×U_w with pairwise distinct x_i and arbitrary v_i; the input order is unrestricted. On query q∈U_w the output is (1,v_i) if q=x_i and (0,0) if q is absent. The stored set and values do not change after construction. The machine is a sequential word RAM with w-bit registers and cells. The primitive unit-cost instructions are memory reads and writes, copies, comparisons, conditional branches, addition and subtraction modulo 2ʷ, multiplication returning the full product in two words, integer quotient and remainder of two words with nonzero divisor, bitwise Boolean operations, and logical shifts. A shift by at least w returns zero; otherwise shifted-out bits are discarded. Addresses may occupy a fixed number of words, and all operations computing them are charged. Programs have finitely many instructions and constants, may receive n and w, and contain no input-size or word-size advice, random instruction, free table or special hashing primitive. Every table, parameter computation, memory initialization and output write performed by construction counts toward its time; input storage, the resulting dictionary and temporary storage count toward its space. Query reads the constructed representation and may use temporary workspace, with every operation charged; all retained information about the input is in the counted representation. The query must be correct on every q, including absent keys. Programs and constants may depend on d but not on n, w, the input or query. This spells out the saved w=Θ(log n) convention as a claim for every fixed polynomial-size universe; Pagh’s broader arbitrary-word-length formulation is not asserted equivalent here.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the proposition with deterministic algorithms meeting all three bounds for every fixed d, or disprove it for at least one fixed d. The negation says that no pair of admissible correct programs has simultaneously linear worst-case construction time, linear total space and constant worst-case query time for all inputs in that word-length range. Failure of a particular hash family, an average-input lower bound, or a lower bound in a comparison-only model is not that negation.

cards.title: Can all pairwise sums X+Y be sorted in quadratic time?
cards.formal: Does there exist a uniform deterministic real-RAM algorithm A and a constant C such that, for every integer n≥2 and every X=(x₁,…,xₙ), Y=(y₁,…,yₙ)∈ℝⁿ, A outputs a permutation ((i₁,j₁),…,(i_{n²},j_{n²})) of [n]×[n] satisfying x_{i_r}+y_{j_r}≤x_{i_{r+1}}+y_{j_{r+1}} for 1≤r<n², in at most Cn² unit-cost operations?
cards.definitions: The input consists of n and the 2n exact real numbers in random-access arrays; no sortedness, distinctness, integrality or magnitude bound is promised. All n² index pairs must occur once in the output, including pairs with equal sums. Ties may appear in any order. A real RAM has exact real registers and cells, supporting copy, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by nonzero reals and comparisons at unit cost. A fixed finite program may use rational constants, with no advice depending on n. It also has integer registers and cells of b=d⌈log₂(n+2)⌉ bits for some fixed integer d≥3 chosen with the algorithm. Integer instructions are copy, comparison, branching, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo 2ᵇ, quotient and remainder with nonzero divisor, bitwise Boolean operations, and logical shifts; shifts by at least b return zero. Integer addresses access individual real or integer cells, and each read or write costs one operation. Integer-to-real conversion is permitted, but real-to-integer conversion, floor on reals, extraction of their bits and arbitrary-precision integer operations are not primitives. Memory starts empty apart from the input and fixed program constants; all preprocessing, table construction, address computation and output writes are charged. The algorithm must halt correctly on every input and uses no randomness. Constants C and d are independent of n and of the real values. This is the quadratic-time real-RAM version explicitly asked in the cited necklace paper and identified as the main target in TOPP. Indexed multiset output resolves possible equal sums; allowing repeated input entries does not change the target, since repetitions can be grouped by O(n log n) comparison sorting and expanded within the output budget.
cards.answer_criterion: Give one uniform deterministic program with a proof of exact output correctness and the O(n²) worst-case total-time bound for every real input, or prove that no such program exists in the specified model. Equivalently, a negative answer shows that every correct program has unbounded worst-case running-time/n² ratio. Neither a bound only on the number of comparisons nor an algorithm restricted to bounded integers resolves this claim.

cards.title: Does P equal NP?
cards.formal: Does every language with polynomially bounded, polynomial-time verifiable certificates admit a deterministic polynomial-time decision algorithm? Equivalently, do there exist a deterministic Turing machine A and constants C,k such that, for every encoded Boolean formula F of bit length n, A decides whether F has a satisfying assignment and halts within $C(n+1)^k$ steps? The algorithm must give the correct answer on every input.
cards.definitions: A language is a subset of the finite binary strings. P consists of languages decided by one deterministic multitape Turing machine with worst-case running time C(n+1)^k for some constants C,k. NP consists of languages L for which there are a deterministic polynomial-time verifier V and a polynomial p satisfying $x\in L\iff\exists y\in\{0,1\}^{\le p(|x|)}:V(x,y)=1$. The verifier's time is polynomial in the combined input length. SAT is the language of well-formed Boolean formulas with at least one satisfying assignment; malformed encodings are rejected. Fix any ordinary explicit binary encoding of formulas using AND, OR, and NOT. The question concerns uniform deterministic computation, with no advice, oracle, or error probability. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove P=NP or P≠NP in the deterministic uniform model defined here. Equality requires that every NP language have a polynomial-time decision algorithm; inequality requires that at least one NP language have none.
cards.status_note: The Clay Mathematics Institute lists P versus NP as unsolved, checked on 11 September 2026. The cited restricted-circuit lower bounds and proof-method barriers do not resolve the uniform decision problem.

cards.title: Does P equal PSPACE?
cards.formal: Does every language decidable by a deterministic Turing machine using polynomial working space have a deterministic polynomial-time decision algorithm? Equivalently, do there exist a machine A and constants C,k such that A decides truth of every closed quantified Boolean formula of encoded length n in at most $C(n+1)^k$ steps?
cards.definitions: P consists of languages decided by one deterministic multitape Turing machine with a fixed polynomial worst-case time bound. PSPACE consists of languages decided by one deterministic Turing machine which halts on every input and visits at most C(n+1)^k work-tape cells, for some constants C,k, on inputs of length n. The input is read-only and is not charged as work space; a fixed finite tape alphabet is used. PSPACE imposes no polynomial time bound. A closed quantified Boolean formula has the form Q₁x₁⋯Qₘxₘ φ(x₁,…,xₘ), where each Qᵢ is ∃ or ∀, quantified variables are distinct, and φ is an explicitly encoded Boolean formula using AND, OR, and NOT, with no free variables. Every quantifier ranges over {0,1}. The number of quantifiers and their alternations may grow with n; the input is not restricted to a fixed number of blocks. Use any standard explicit binary encoding, reject malformed inputs, and count its full bit length n. Truth means the usual nested Boolean quantifier semantics. This language, TQBF, is PSPACE-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. No oracle, advice, randomization, or promise is allowed. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove P=PSPACE or P≠PSPACE. The first outcome asserts a deterministic polynomial-time decision procedure for every polynomial-space language; the second asserts a polynomial-space language with no deterministic polynomial-time decision procedure.
cards.status_note: Primary-source review and a search for subsequent results on 11 September 2026 found no resolution. Williams’ 2025 simulation and August 2026 MFCS survey concern time-space bounds; neither states an equality or separation of P and PSPACE.

cards.title: Is nonuniform TC⁰ strictly smaller than nonuniform NC¹?
cards.formal: Is TC⁰⊊NC¹ for the nonuniform circuit classes defined below? Equivalently, does there exist a Boolean function family f=(f_n:{0,1}^n→{0,1}) in NC¹ such that for every fixed depth d≥1, exponent k≥1, and constant M≥1, there is an n for which every depth-at-most-d majority circuit computing f_n exactly has size greater than M(n+1)^k?
cards.definitions: A circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with input nodes x_1,…,x_n, optional constants 0,1, and one output. Depth is the maximum number of gates on an input-to-output path. Size is the number of gates plus the number of wires; if an input is repeated at a gate, each occurrence counts as a wire. A majority circuit has AND and OR gates of arbitrary positive fan-in, NOT gates of fan-in one, and MAJ gates of arbitrary positive fan-in m, with output 1 exactly when strictly more than m/2 inputs equal 1. TC⁰ consists of all families with such circuits of size M(n+1)^k and depth at most d for every n, for some constants M,k,d depending on the family. NC¹ consists of families with circuits over AND, OR, NOT, with fan-in at most two (one for NOT), size M(n+1)^k, and depth at most b log_2(n+1), for fixed M,k,b. Circuits may share intermediate gates. Both classes are nonuniform: an arbitrary separate circuit may be chosen for each input length, without any requirement to compute its description. The output must be correct on every input; no randomness, approximation, promise, or distributional error is allowed.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove TC⁰⊊NC¹ or TC⁰=NC¹ for the nonuniform families defined here. Strictness requires a single NC¹ family with no polynomial-size constant-depth majority-circuit family; equality requires that every NC¹ family admit such a family.
cards.status_note: The source and subsequent-work checks on 11 September 2026 found no equality or separation of these nonuniform classes. The 2026 depth-two result concerns a function in E^NP and polynomial circuit size; the typed-monoid result concerns uniform classes. These conclusions have different quantifiers and models from the target.

cards.title: The Berman–Hartmanis isomorphism conjecture
cards.formal: For every pair of languages A,B⊆{0,1}* that are NP-complete under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions, does there exist a bijection f:{0,1}*→{0,1}* such that f and f⁻¹ are computable in deterministic polynomial time and, for every string x, x∈A if and only if f(x)∈B?
cards.definitions: A language is a set of finite binary strings, including a specified membership decision for every string; malformed encodings are therefore part of the language convention. NP consists of languages L for which x∈L exactly when some witness of length polynomial in |x| is accepted by a deterministic polynomial-time verifier. A many-one reduction from L to A is a total deterministic polynomial-time function g with x∈L iff g(x)∈A. A is NP-complete if A∈NP and every L∈NP reduces to A in this sense. The desired f is a permutation of all finite binary strings, taking members to members and nonmembers to nonmembers. Its running time is polynomial in its input length, and its inverse has a polynomial bound in the inverse input length. The algorithms and polynomial bounds may depend on the fixed pair A,B, but not on the particular input string. No advice, oracle, randomness or length-preservation requirement is allowed. This is the unconditional conjecture; P≠NP is not an assumption.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove that every pair of polynomial-time many-one NP-complete languages is polynomial-time isomorphic, or prove that some pair has no bijection with both directions computable in polynomial time. The statement is unconditional: P≠NP is not an added hypothesis.
cards.status_note: The 2022 primary-author problem column states that the full conjecture is open. A later-source search on 11 September 2026 located the 2025 recovery-reduction preprint, which still uses it as a conjectural hypothesis, and found no resolution. Its truth-table recovery consequence is conditional.

cards.title: Černý conjecture: a reset word of length at most (n−1)²
cards.formal: Does every synchronizing complete deterministic finite automaton with n≥1 states have a reset word of length at most (n−1)²?
cards.definitions: An automaton here is a finite transition system A=(Q,Σ,δ), with |Q|=n, a finite nonempty alphabet Σ, and a total function δ:Q×Σ→Q. Extend δ to words by δ(q,ε)=q and δ(q,wa)=δ(δ(q,w),a). A word w is a reset word when |{δ(q,w):q∈Q}|=1. The automaton is synchronizing if at least one such word exists; its reset threshold rt(A) is the minimum number of letters in a reset word. The quantification ranges over every n and every finite alphabet and total transition function satisfying this promise. The common final state need not be specified beforehand. Initial states and accepting states play no role. The empty word handles n=1. No strong-connectivity, binary-alphabet, permutation-letter, or other structural restriction is imposed. Partial automata, nondeterministic transitions, and synchronizing only a prescribed proper subset of Q are different models.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove that rt(A)≤(n−1)² for every synchronizing complete deterministic n-state automaton, or exhibit such an automaton with rt(A)>(n−1)² and prove that strict inequality. Alphabets and state counts are unrestricted as specified above.

cards.title: Can every two-way NFA be determinized with polynomially many states?
cards.formal: Do universal constants C,k≥1 exist such that, for every n≥1, every finite nonempty input alphabet Σ and every two-way nondeterministic finite automaton A over Σ with at most n states, there is a two-way deterministic finite automaton D over the same alphabet with at most C(n+1)^k states satisfying L(D)=L(A)? Equivalence must hold on all finite input words, without a length bound.
cards.definitions: The read-only input tape contains a left endmarker, a word w∈Σ*, and a right endmarker. Each automaton has one head, initially on the left endmarker, a finite set Q of states with a designated initial state and designated halting accepting states. In each nonhalting configuration it uses its current state and the scanned symbol to choose a new state and a head displacement in {−1,0,+1}; moves outside the endmarkers are forbidden. A missing transition rejects that branch. A word is accepted if some finite computation reaches an accepting state. Infinite nonaccepting branches do not count as acceptance. For a deterministic automaton there is at most one available transition in each state-symbol pair, and its unique infinite run, if any, rejects. There is no work tape, rewritable input, second head, stack, counter, randomness or advice. State count includes all control and halting states, but the bound is independent of word length and alphabet size. The target is existence of D for each A; computing D from A is not required to take polynomial time. Standard endmarker and stay-put conventions change these state bounds only by polynomial factors.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the existence of universal constants C,k giving an equivalent 2DFA with at most C(n+1)^k states for every n-state 2NFA, or prove that no such constants exist. In the negative direction, every proposed polynomial bound must fail on some source automaton; all language comparisons concern words of every length.

Adeogun and Kapoutsis’ July 2026 revision supplies a quadratic lower bound, still compatible with polynomial determinization. cards.title: Does any regular language require generalized star height greater than one?
cards.formal: Does there exist a finite nonempty alphabet Σ and a regular language L⊆Σ* such that every generalized regular expression denoting L has Kleene-star nesting depth at least two, when complement is allowed without increasing that depth?
cards.definitions: Σ* is the set of all finite words over Σ, including the empty word ε. A regular language is one accepted by a finite deterministic automaton. Generalized expressions are finite expressions built from ∅, ε, and the letters a∈Σ using binary union E∪F, concatenation EF, complement E^c, and Kleene star E*. Their meanings are respectively the empty language, {ε}, {a}, language union, all concatenations uv with u∈L(E) and v∈L(F), Σ*∖L(E), and the union of all finite concatenation powers of L(E), including power zero {ε}. Set h(∅)=h(ε)=h(a)=0, h(E∪F)=h(EF)=max{h(E),h(F)}, h(E^c)=h(E), and h(E*)=h(E)+1. Define h_g(L)=min{h(E):L(E)=L}, which exists because every regular language has an ordinary regular expression. The question is whether h_g(L)>1 for at least one such L. There is no bound on expression size, number of complements, union or concatenation depth, automaton size, or alphabet size. Intersection is permitted as the abbreviation (E^c∪F^c)^c and does not add star depth. Backreferences, infinite words, additional predicates and auxiliary alphabets in the final expression are not part of the syntax.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove that some regular language has generalized star height at least two, including a lower bound over all generalized expressions for that language, or prove that every regular language over every finite nonempty alphabet has a generalized expression of star height at most one. Expression size is unrestricted in both alternatives.

cards.title: Decidability of every level of the dot-depth hierarchy
cards.formal: For every fixed integer k≥0, is there an algorithm that, given a deterministic finite automaton over a finite alphabet A, always halts and decides whether its language belongs to DD_k(A), the k-th dot-depth level defined below?
cards.definitions: For each finite nonempty alphabet A, let A* be its finite words, ε the empty word, and A+=A*∖{ε}. Set DD₀(A)={∅,{ε},A+,A*}. For a class C of languages over A, Pol(C) consists of all finite unions of marked products L₀a₁L₁⋯a_rL_r, where r≥0, each a_i∈A, and every L_i∈C; r=0 gives L₀. Let Bool(C) be closure under finite union, finite intersection and complement relative to A*. Define DD_{k+1}(A)=Bool(Pol(DD_k(A))). The input automaton is given by finite explicit tables, including its alphabet, initial state and accepting states; its accepted language is L(M). The question quantifies ∀k∃a total Turing algorithm A_k∀M, with A_k(M)=yes exactly when L(M)∈DD_k(A). Each A_k must handle arbitrary finite input alphabets. No polynomial-time or elementary-time bound is requested. This fixes the full integer levels and the four-language level-zero convention; it does not merge distinct concatenation hierarchies or leave the logical signature implicit. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.

cards.title: Equivalence of deterministic macro tree transducers
cards.formal: Is there a total algorithm that, given two deterministic macro tree transducers with the same finite ranked input and output alphabets, decides whether they define exactly the same partial function from finite ordered input trees to finite ordered output trees?
cards.definitions: Fix the ordinary inside-out, or call-by-value, semantics. A ranked alphabet assigns a nonnegative arity to each symbol; a tree node has exactly that many ordered children. A transducer has finitely many states q, each with one input-tree argument and m(q) output-tree parameters, and an initial state q₀ with m(q₀)=0. For each state q and input symbol σ of arity k there is at most one rule q(σ(x₁,…,x_k),y₁,…,y_m)→r. The finite right-hand side follows the grammar r ::= y_j | δ(r₁,…,r_l) | q′(x_i,r₁,…,r_{m(q′)}), with δ an output symbol of arity l and 1≤i≤k. Subtrees and parameters may be copied or deleted, and calls may be nested inside parameter arguments without a fixed nesting bound across instances. On input σ(t₁,…,t_k), evaluate parameter arguments to output trees, then evaluate a call q′ on the indicated child t_i with those parameter values. A missing rule makes the corresponding evaluation undefined, and under call-by-value an undefined argument makes its enclosing evaluation undefined. There is no inspection or pattern matching on parameter trees. Every recursive call processes a proper input child, so evaluation terminates on each finite input, with either a finite tree or undefined. A transducer with a rule for every state/symbol pair is total. There is no regular look-ahead oracle in this chosen syntax. Equality requires identical domains and, on that domain, identical labelled ordered output trees, without identifying different trees by their leaf strings, shapes or origin annotations. Input alphabets, state sets, arities and rules are all part of the finite input to the desired decision algorithm.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove that equivalence of the specified partial deterministic macro tree transducers is decidable by a total algorithm, or prove that this decision problem is undecidable. Equivalence requires equality of domains and of the labelled ordered output trees on every input in the common domain.

cards.title: Is positivity of integer linear recurrences decidable?
cards.formal: Does there exist a Turing machine that, on every input consisting of an integer d≥1, integer initial values u_0,…,u_{d−1}, and integer coefficients a_0,…,a_{d−1}, halts and decides whether u_n≥0 for every n≥0, where u_{n+d}=sum_{i=0}^{d−1}a_i u_{n+i}? The order d is part of the input and has no fixed upper bound.
cards.definitions: All integers are given exactly in signed binary, and the coefficient and initial-value lists are explicit. The recurrence is homogeneous and its coefficients are constant in n. The requested property includes every term from u_0 onward and allows zero terms. Coefficients may be zero, including a_0; the decision procedure must accept these inputs as well. No promise of distinct characteristic roots, reversibility, eventual nonnegativity, or bounded order is imposed. The recurrence supplied need not be of minimal order. Computation uses the ordinary Turing model, with no real-number or number-theoretic oracle. No polynomial-time or other specified running-time bound is required, but the machine must halt for both possible answers. A simple sequence has a minimal characteristic polynomial with no repeated complex roots. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.

cards.title: Can simple stochastic games be solved in polynomial time?
cards.formal: Is the following decision problem in deterministic polynomial time? Given an explicitly represented finite simple stochastic game G, a start vertex s, and a binary rational threshold r∈[0,1], decide whether v_G(s)>r, where v_G(s)=sup_σ inf_τ Pr_s^{σ,τ}[eventually reach the target sink 1]. The game and threshold follow the exact conventions below, and time is polynomial in their total bit length.
cards.definitions: The vertices are partitioned into Max, Min, random, and two distinct terminal sinks 0 and 1. Every nonterminal vertex has two listed successor slots; slots may have the same successor. At a Max or Min vertex its owner chooses a slot. At a random vertex each slot is chosen with probability 1/2, independently at each visit. Both players observe the complete finite history and the current vertex. Strategies may use history and private randomness; there is no bound on play length. Reaching 1 gives Max payoff one; reaching 0, or playing forever without reaching 1, gives payoff zero. Min minimizes the same expected payoff that Max maximizes. No promise of almost-sure termination is imposed. All vertices, ownership labels and successor indices are explicit; r=a/b is exact with binary integers 0≤a≤b and b>0. Equality v_G(s)=r is a NO instance. The algorithm is an ordinary uniform deterministic Turing algorithm; its polynomial bound has universal constants independent of the game and threshold. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove that the exact threshold language {(G,s,r):v_G(s)>r} belongs to P, or prove that it does not. The polynomial-time algorithm must handle arbitrary finite games, including nonterminating plays, and reject equality to the threshold.

cards.title: An internal tower of semisimplicial types in ordinary HoTT
cards.formal: In the fixed ordinary HoTT theory T below, can one define a single internal family S:ℕ→U₁ and restriction maps r_n:S(n+1)→S(n) whose finite stages are equivalent, compatibly with restriction, to the canonical finite semisimplicial telescopes D_n?
cards.definitions: Fix T to be intensional Martin–Löf type theory with dependent function and pair types Π,Σ, identity types with their J eliminator, empty and unit types, finite coproducts, natural numbers and W-types, a cumulative predicative sequence U₀:U₁:⋯ closed under these constructors, and univalence for these universes. Also allow propositional truncation and homotopy pushouts with their ordinary dependent eliminators and propositional computation rules for path constructors, as in the HoTT book. There is no equality reflection, axiom K/UIP, resizing, choice, excluded middle, second equality type, display modality, or additional primitive for semisimplicial types. The question concerns definability in this specified theory; a negative result would apply to this theory, not automatically to every possible extension called HoTT. Define an external, finite family of syntactic telescopes as follows. D₀ is U₀, with element A₀. Given data d=(A₀,…,A_{j−1}) in D_{j−1}, form B_j(d), the dependent type of labelled boundaries of a j-simplex: for every nonempty proper subset F of {0,…,j}, in increasing cardinality and then lexicographic order, choose a label x_F in A_{|F|−1} evaluated on the labels of all nonempty proper subfaces of F. Identify F with {0,…,|F|−1} by its increasing enumeration when supplying these arguments. For singleton F this means x_F:A₀. Set D_j=Σ(d:D_{j−1})(B_j(d)→U₀), whose last field is A_j, and let p_j:D_{j+1}→D_j forget the last field. This describes an ordinary finite T-expression for each external integer j; it does not postulate an internal function j↦D_j. The required output is finite closed T-terms S:ℕ→U₁ and r:Π(n:ℕ)(S(n+1)→S(n)), together with a metatheoretic proof that for every external j there are T-terms e_j:S(j)≃D_j and homotopies e_j∘r_j ~ p_j∘e_{j+1}. Here j inside T denotes its numeral, ≃ is the usual type equivalence, and ~ is pointwise identity. No judgmental equality between S(j) and D_j is required. The equivalences classify the full type-valued telescopes, with arbitrary U₀-small simplex types and no fixed truncation bound.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove that the specified theory T admits finite closed terms S and r together with the external stagewise equivalences and compatibility homotopies required above, or prove that no such terms and witnesses exist in T. The positive conclusion must hold at every external finite stage and allow arbitrary U₀-small simplex types.

cards.title: Can a Scott-continuous lambda model validate exactly beta-conversion?
cards.formal: Does there exist a pointed directed-complete partial order D and Scott-continuous maps F:D→[D→D] and L:[D→D]→D with F∘L=id such that, for every pair of finite untyped lambda terms M,N, equality of their interpretations for every environment in D holds if and only if M and N are beta-convertible?
cards.definitions: Terms are generated by variables from a countably infinite set, application MN and abstraction λx.M, modulo renaming bound variables. Beta-convertibility is the least equivalence relation closed under application and abstraction containing (λx.M)N=M[N/x], with capture-avoiding substitution. A directed set is nonempty and every two of its elements have an upper bound in the set. D is a set with a partial order, a least element, and a supremum for every directed subset. Scott-continuous means monotone and preserving directed suprema. [D→D] consists of all Scott-continuous functions, ordered pointwise. An environment ρ assigns an element of D to each variable. Interpret x as ρ(x), MN as F(⟦M⟧ρ)(⟦N⟧ρ), and λx.M as L(d↦⟦M⟧(ρ[x:=d])). The desired condition is ∀M,N: (∀ρ, ⟦M⟧ρ=⟦N⟧ρ) ⇔ M=βN. Models need not be countable, algebraic, effectively presented or extensional; in particular L∘F=id is not required. These are set-based directed-complete orders and all their continuous maps, without a restriction to graph models.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove that a pointed dcpo and continuous retraction F,L satisfying the stated exact-theory condition exist, or prove that none exist. A negative answer must cover all such dcpos, without assuming an effective presentation, algebraicity or extensionality.

cards.title: Does weak normalization imply strong normalization for every pure type system?
cards.formal: For every pure type system (S,A,R) defined below, does weak normalization of every typable term imply strong normalization of every typable term?
cards.definitions: S is a set of sorts, A⊆S×S is a set of axioms, and R⊆S×S×S is a set of product rules. Terms are finite expressions t ::= x | s | t u | λx:B.t | Πx:B.C, with s∈S and variables from a countably infinite set, modulo renaming bound variables. A context is a finite sequence of declarations of distinct variables. Typing is the least relation Γ⊢t:B generated by the following rules. Axiom: ∅⊢s:t when (s,t)∈A. Start: Γ,x:B⊢x:B when Γ⊢B:s and x is fresh. Weakening: Γ,x:C⊢t:B when Γ⊢t:B, Γ⊢C:s and x is fresh. Product: Γ⊢Πx:B.C:s₃ when Γ⊢B:s₁, Γ,x:B⊢C:s₂ and (s₁,s₂,s₃)∈R. Abstraction: Γ⊢λx:B.t:Πx:B.C when Γ,x:B⊢t:C and Γ⊢Πx:B.C:s for a sort s. Application: Γ⊢t u:C[u/x] when Γ⊢t:Πx:B.C and Γ⊢u:B. Conversion: Γ⊢t:C when Γ⊢t:B, Γ⊢C:s and B=βC. All substitutions avoid capture. A beta step contracts (λx:B.t)u to t[u/x] at any subterm, including inside annotations and product types. =β is the reflexive, symmetric, transitive closure of those steps. A term is typable if Γ⊢t:B for some finite Γ,B. Weak normalization means that each typable term has some finite beta-reduction sequence ending in a term with no beta redex. Strong normalization means that no typable term starts an infinite beta-reduction sequence. Both predicates quantify over open as well as closed terms and over all their reduction choices. The sets S,A,R need not be finite, decidable or functional.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove that every pure type system in which all typable terms are weakly beta-normalizing is strongly beta-normalizing, or exhibit a pure type system that is weakly normalizing for every typable term but has a typable term admitting an infinite beta-reduction sequence.
cards.status_note: The primary statement and Mull’s 2023 paper leave the unrestricted conjecture open. A later-result and author-publication search on 11 September 2026 found no general proof or counterexample. The positive theorems impose additional PTS structure.

cards.title: Can every polynomial-time decision problem be efficiently parallelized?
cards.formal: Is P=NC, where NC consists of decision languages recognized by logspace-uniform Boolean circuit families of polynomial size and polylogarithmic depth? Equivalently, does the Circuit Value Problem have such a circuit family?
cards.definitions: P is deterministic polynomial time on ordinary Turing machines. For L∈NC there must be fixed constants c,k,C and a family (Cₙ)ₙ≥0 such that Cₙ decides membership in L correctly on every n-bit input, has at most C(n+2)ᶜ gates, and has depth at most C(log₂(n+2))ᵏ. Gates are two-input AND and OR and one-input NOT; fan-out is unrestricted and one output bit is designated. Depth is the longest input-to-output gate path. A deterministic O(log(n+2))-space transducer given 1ⁿ must output the description of Cₙ; its polynomial output bound is part of the size requirement. Constants and the generator may depend on L but not on n. Circuit Value receives an explicit topologically ordered Boolean gate DAG, its input-bit values, and an output-gate index; it asks whether that gate evaluates to 1. Its input length n is the entire binary encoding length, and malformed encodings are rejected. No randomization, advice, oracle, or restriction to monotone gates is permitted. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.

cards.formal: Does there exist an integer c≥2 such that, for every fixed integer d≥2, a uniform randomized LOCAL algorithm A_d and a constant K_d solve every n-event variable Lovász Local Lemma instance of dependency degree at most d and maximum bad-event probability p with p·d^c<1/2, within K_d(1+log₂log₂(n+2)) rounds, with probability at least 1−n^(−3) of avoiding all bad events simultaneously?
cards.definitions: There are n≥2 bad events, each a predicate on a specified finite subset of finitely many mutually independent variables. Each variable has a finite nonempty alphabet and a rational probability distribution; event predicates and distributions are given by finite tables. Variables occurring in no event can be omitted. Two distinct event nodes are adjacent exactly when their variable sets intersect; this graph is the communication network. Its maximum degree is at most d. The number p is the largest probability of an event under the product of the specified distributions. Each node initially knows n,d, its own event table, its variables and their distributions, its neighbours and their identifiers. Node identifiers are distinct integers in [n²]; shared variables have consistent names. LOCAL means synchronous rounds with arbitrarily long finite messages in each direction on each edge, and unrestricted terminating local computation. Nodes have private independent fair random bits. A single finite program is used at all nodes, independently of n and the instance. Each node outputs one value for each of its variables. Success requires agreement on shared variables and falsity of every event. The round bound holds on every random tape; the success probability is over all node coins for each fixed instance and identifier assignment. Constants and the algorithm may depend on d; the slack exponent c is chosen before d. No preprocessing using the full instance is supplied. The factor 1/2 removes the low-degree ambiguity recorded in the source conjecture.

cards.title: Optimal exact single-source shortest paths in CONGEST
cards.formal: For every fixed integer b≥1, do there exist constants K,c>0 and a uniform randomized CONGEST algorithm which, on every connected simple undirected graph with n≥2 vertices, integer edge weights in [0,n^b] and a designated source s, makes every vertex output its exact weighted distance from s in at most K(√n+D)(log₂(n+2))^c rounds on every execution, with simultaneous correctness probability at least 1−n^(−3)? Here D is the diameter of the unweighted graph.
cards.definitions: A path length is the sum of its edge weights; the distance is the minimum path length, and the source distance is zero. D is the maximum over vertex pairs of the minimum number of edges on a path between them. The graph itself is the network. In each synchronous round, each endpoint of each edge can send at most B⌈log₂(n+2)⌉ bits to the other endpoint, for a constant B depending only on b. Nodes initially know n,b, the source identifier, their own identifiers, and the identifiers and weights of incident neighbours. Identifiers are distinct integers in [n²]. Local computation and memory are unrestricted, but each local computation between rounds terminates. Nodes use independent private fair random bits. One finite program, allowed to depend on b, runs at all nodes; no global graph description, advice, routing tables or preprocessing is supplied. The graph, weights, source and identifiers are fixed before randomness is drawn. Output at v is an ordinary binary integer for dist(s,v), stored locally. The guarantee concerns all vertices together, over all coins. All communication, including finding termination and any preprocessing, counts in the round bound. K,c,B are independent of n,D and the instance; no value of D is initially supplied.

cards.title: Does general rational linear programming have a strongly polynomial algorithm?
cards.formal: Does there exist a deterministic algorithm, with fixed polynomials p and q, that solves every rational linear program $\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}$, where A has m rows and n columns, using at most p(m+n) elementary arithmetic, comparison, and data-transfer operations, while every intermediate rational number has binary encoding length at most q(N)? Here N is the total input bit length. Solving means returning an exact optimal rational solution if one exists, or correctly reporting infeasibility or an objective unbounded below.
cards.definitions: A is in Q^(m by n), b in Q^m, and c in Q^n, with m,n>=1. All coefficients are supplied explicitly as binary signed numerators and positive denominators. No full-rank, nondegeneracy, strict-feasibility, coefficient-size, or conditioning promise is made. Elementary scalar operations are addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by a nonzero quantity, comparisons, and transfers of stored values. The program is fixed and finite; no oracle, advice, randomization, floor operation, or uncharged access to binary digits is allowed. Rational encoding length means the bit length of a numerator-denominator representation. The polynomial p is independent of N and of every coefficient magnitude; q may depend on N. Consequently the algorithm must also admit a polynomial-time bit implementation. The output is a solution vector, not a required optimal basis. Infeasible means that the feasible set is empty; unbounded means it is nonempty and the infimum of c^T x is minus infinity. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.

cards.title: Does the packing property imply the max-flow min-cut property?
cards.formal: Does every finite clutter with the packing property have the max-flow min-cut property? Equivalently, if every deletion/contraction minor satisfies unweighted integral packing–covering equality, must weighted integral packing–covering equality hold for every nonnegative integer weight vector?
cards.definitions: A clutter C on a finite ground set E is a family of subsets of E, no one properly containing another. In the original instance all members are nonempty; the empty family is allowed. A cover T⊆E meets every member, and τ(C) is the smallest cover size. A packing is a family of pairwise disjoint members, with maximum size ν(C). Deleting e removes e from the ground set and discards all members containing e. Contracting e removes it from the ground set and from every member, and retains only inclusion-minimal resulting members. A minor results from any sequence of these operations. The packing property means τ(C′)=ν(C′) for every minor C′. For the empty family both values are zero; for a minor containing the empty set both are defined as +∞, with the empty member permitted arbitrarily many times in a packing. For w∈ℤ_{≥0}^E, let τ_w(C)=min{Σ_{e∈T}w_e:T covers C}. Let ν_w(C) be the maximum of Σ_{F∈C}y_F over nonnegative integers y_F satisfying Σ_{F∋e}y_F≤w_e for every e∈E. Thus a weighted packing may use a member repeatedly, subject to capacities w. The max-flow min-cut property is τ_w(C)=ν_w(C) for every such w. The original nonempty-member assumption makes these weighted optima finite.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove that the packing property implies τ_w=ν_w for every finite clutter and every nonnegative integer weight vector, or give a finite clutter and weight vector with the packing property and τ_w>ν_w. A counterexample must verify equality for all minors, not merely for the original unweighted clutter. Finite searches, proofs for a proper subclass, or fractional optimality alone do not resolve the universal statement.

cards.title: Nearly linear-time solution of general sparse linear systems
cards.formal: For every fixed integer c≥1, does there exist a uniform randomized classical algorithm A_c with the following guarantee? Given n≥2, a nonsingular rational n×n matrix A with m nonzero entries, a nonzero rational vector b, and an integer 1≤p≤c·ceil(log_2 n), output a rational vector x̂ such that ||Ax̂−b||_2≤2^(−p)||b||_2 with probability at least 2/3. Each numerator and positive denominator of A and b has at most c·ceil(log_2 n) binary digits, and the spectral condition number κ_2(A) is promised at most n^c. The worst-case running time must be O_c(m log^(d_c)n) for some constant d_c independent of the input.
cards.definitions: The input lists the row index, column index and rational value of each nonzero coefficient, without duplicate positions, together with the n entries of b; hence n≤m≤n². The Euclidean norm is ||v||_2=(Σ_i v_i²)^(1/2), and κ_2(A)=σ_max(A)/σ_min(A), the ratio of its largest and smallest singular values. Nonsingularity makes the denominator positive. A may be nonsymmetric, indefinite and unrelated to a graph Laplacian. The algorithm need only meet its guarantee on promised inputs; it is not asked to certify the condition-number promise. Computation uses a word RAM with Θ(log n)-bit words, conventional arithmetic, comparison, bit operations and memory access; all operations on longer numbers, preprocessing, random-bit generation and writing the output are charged. No operation on an arbitrary real number has unit cost. Converting word operations to bit operations changes only polylogarithmic factors. Constants and the fixed program may depend on c, but neither nonuniform advice depending on n nor a supplied inverse or preconditioner is allowed. Here ε=2^(−p); this is the polynomial-condition, inverse-polynomial-accuracy regime of the near-input-size target. The output is the full list of n rational coordinates, each as a signed binary numerator and positive binary denominator; every output bit is charged. The word instructions are random-access reads/writes, comparisons, conditional branches, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo 2^w, integer quotient/remainder with nonzero divisor, bitwise Boolean operations, and shifts of a w-bit word; shifts by at least w yield zero. The constant in word length w=Θ(log n) (or Θ(log N) when N is the stated input size) is fixed with the algorithm. Address arithmetic has the same cost, larger integers occupy multiple words, and no instruction performs arbitrary-precision arithmetic in one step. When randomization is allowed, a fresh independent uniform w-bit word costs one operation.

cards.title: Smale’s seventh problem
cards.formal: Do there exist constants C,K>0, an integer k≥1 and a deterministic real-number algorithm A in the model below such that, for every integer N≥2, A(N) outputs N distinct points x₁,…,x_N on S² in at most KN^k operations and E_N(x₁,…,x_N)≤E_N*+C ln N?
cards.definitions: S²={x∈ℝ³: x₁²+x₂²+x₃²=1}. The energy is E_N(x₁,…,x_N)=Σ_{i≠j}−ln‖x_i−x_j‖₂, counting ordered pairs; collisions have energy +∞. E_N* is the infimum over all N-tuples on S². ln is the natural logarithm and ‖·‖₂ is Euclidean distance. The algorithm is one finite real-arithmetic program with a fixed finite list of real constants, independent of N. It has exact real registers and a finite-control tape machine with register copying, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by a nonzero register, and branching on the sign of a register. Tape movements and each scalar arithmetic, comparison or copy operation have unit cost. Input is the integer N as an exact real value; output is a list of 3N real coordinates. Any finite tape/register storage used by the program is charged through its operations. There is no primitive logarithm, square root, floor, random sample or minimization oracle. Polynomial time is in N, not in log N. The inequality is a mathematical condition on the output; the algorithm need not evaluate the energy. This specifies the real-number computation convention in Smale’s problem; coordinates need not be rational and no bit-cost bound is asserted.

cards.title: Does every isotropic log-concave measure have a dimension-free Poincaré constant?
cards.formal: Does there exist a universal constant C<∞ such that, for every dimension n≥1, every isotropic log-concave probability measure μ on ℝⁿ, and every locally Lipschitz f:ℝⁿ→ℝ with finite second moment and finite gradient energy, $\operatorname{Var}_\mu(f)\le C\int\|\nabla f(x)\|_2^2\,d\mu(x)$? This is the Poincaré formulation of the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture.
cards.definitions: The measure has a Lebesgue density ρ=e^{−V}, where V:ℝⁿ→ℝ∪{+∞} is convex and ∫ρ=1; allowing V=+∞ includes uniform distributions on full-dimensional convex bodies. Isotropy means ∫x dμ(x)=0 and ∫xxᵀ dμ(x)=Iₙ. Variance is Varμ(f)=∫(f−∫f dμ)²dμ, and ∇f is the almost-everywhere Euclidean gradient. Let C_P(μ) be the infimum of constants that make the displayed inequality hold for all the stated f. The requested bound is supₙ supμ C_P(μ)<∞, with μ ranging over isotropic log-concave measures in ℝⁿ. There is no symmetry, product structure, smoothness, or positive lower curvature bound on V. The universal constant may depend on none of n, μ, or f. In the isoperimetric convention used by the recent papers, ψμ is the reciprocal Cheeger expansion constant; ψμ² is comparable to C_P(μ) up to universal factors. Thus a bound on ψμ must be squared when expressed as a bound on the Poincaré constant used here.

Tracing the opposite pairs must give one component. A separate constant-size encoding represents the crossing-free circle. The embedding is required to be a valid sphere embedding; malformed encodings may be rejected by polynomial-time combinatorial checks. If the diagram has n crossings, a standard such encoding has O(n log(n+1)) bits. The complexity parameter is the supplied encoding length N, not the minimum crossing number among equivalent diagrams. The input is explicit rather than a compressed description of an exponentially larger diagram. No disk, simplification sequence, knot invariant, auxiliary advice or promise of triviality is supplied. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.

cards.title: Polynomial Hirsch conjecture for edge-path diameter

cards.title: Do one-way functions imply public-key encryption in the standard model?
cards.formal: Does the existence of a classical cryptographic one-way function imply the existence of a classical public-key encryption scheme with negligible correctness error and security against uniform probabilistic polynomial-time chosen-plaintext adversaries? A function ν(n) is negligible if for every d>0 it is eventually at most n^{−d}. The scheme comprises uniform classical polynomial-time algorithms Gen, Enc, Dec. Gen(1ⁿ) randomly outputs public and secret bit strings (pk,sk); Enc(1ⁿ,pk,b) randomly encrypts a bit b; Dec(1ⁿ,sk,c) deterministically outputs a bit or failure. For each b, the probability over honest generation and encryption that decryption is wrong is negligible. Security means that for every uniform classical PPT adversary A, in the experiment (pk,sk)←Gen(1ⁿ), b←{0,1}, c←Enc(1ⁿ,pk,b), the advantage |Pr[A(1ⁿ,pk,c)=b]−1/2| is negligible. The adversary knows all algorithms and can encrypt arbitrary chosen bits itself with fresh randomness. This bit-message formulation extends to polynomially long messages by independent bit encryption and a hybrid argument. All runtime bounds are worst-case polynomial in the security parameter and appropriate input lengths. There is no shared secret before key generation, trusted setup, random oracle, quantum state, or auxiliary hardness assumption. Security is eventually negligible at all sufficiently large parameters, not merely infinitely often.

cards.title: Does P≠NP imply the existence of one-way functions?
cards.formal: Does P≠NP imply that there exists a deterministic polynomial-time computable function f:{0,1}*→{0,1}* such that, for every uniform probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm I and every constant c>0, all sufficiently large n satisfy $\Pr_{x\sim U_n,\,I}[\,|z|=n\ \land\ f(z)=f(x)\,]\le n^{-c}$, where $z\leftarrow I(1^n,f(x))$?
cards.definitions: Uₙ is the uniform distribution on n-bit strings. The function f is computed by one deterministic Turing machine in worst-case polynomial time; in particular its output length is polynomially bounded in n. The inverter receives n in unary and the output f(x), uses independent unbiased random bits, and runs in worst-case polynomial time in the length of its input on every random tape. Its output may be an n-bit candidate or failure. Finding any n-bit preimage counts as success, not only recovering the original x. The probability includes both the choice of x and the inverter’s coins. Formally, for every fixed inverter I and real c>0 there exists N(I,c) such that the inequality holds for every n≥N(I,c). This is eventual negligible inversion probability, not security only at infinitely many lengths. Algorithms have no oracle, nonuniform advice, trapdoor, or quantum computation. The premise P≠NP concerns ordinary uniform deterministic polynomial-time decision versus polynomial-time verification. The task is an existence implication and does not require a black-box construction or a particular proof method.

cards.title: Does ordinary polynomial-hard LWE suffice for circuit obfuscation?
cards.formal: Does the decisional LWE assumption with the fixed polynomial parameters below imply the existence of indistinguishability obfuscation for all polynomial-size Boolean circuits, with no additional hardness, leakage-resilience, or circular-security assumption? The target is a classical polynomial-time obfuscator secure against classical polynomial-size adversaries.
cards.definitions: Fix q(n) to be the least prime at least n^4 for every integer n≥2. Let χ_n be the discrete Gaussian on Z with probability of e proportional to exp(−πe²/n²). The assumed LWE statement is: for every polynomial m(n), the ensembles (A,A s+e mod q) and (A,u) are computationally indistinguishable, where A is uniform in Z_q^(m×n), s is uniform in Z_q^n, the m coordinates of e are independent χ_n samples, and u is independent uniform in Z_q^m. Indistinguishable means every polynomial-size classical circuit family has negligible advantage in n; negligible means smaller than n^(−c) eventually for every constant c>0. No secret-dependent leakage is supplied. An obfuscator O is a uniform probabilistic algorithm running in time polynomial in λ+|C| that outputs a Boolean circuit O(1^λ,C) of polynomial size. Circuits are finite acyclic AND/OR/NOT circuits with fan-in at most two, a specified list of input and output bits, and explicit binary descriptions; |C| is description length. For every polynomial p, there is negligible μ_p such that for every |C|≤p(λ), with probability at least 1−μ_p(λ) over the obfuscator’s coins the output circuit agrees with C on ALL inputs. For every pair of circuit sequences C_0,λ and C_1,λ with polynomially bounded, equal description lengths, the same input/output lengths and identical functions, their obfuscations are computationally indistinguishable against all polynomial-size circuit families. Both functionality and security quantify over all such circuits, without requiring an efficiently checkable proof of equivalence. There is no oracle, trusted setup, quantum state, or restriction to a special circuit family. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.

cards.title: Unleveled fully homomorphic encryption from LWE alone
cards.formal: Does ordinary polynomial-modulus decisional LWE, with the parameter convention below, imply a classical compact fully homomorphic encryption scheme whose keys are generated without an evaluation-depth bound, secure against nonuniform polynomial-size adversaries without any additional circular-security or key-dependent-message assumption?
cards.definitions: Fix the following ordinary LWE assumption: for every fixed integer c≥3 and polynomial sample count M(d), let q(d) be the least prime at least d^c, let s be uniform in Z_q^d, let A be uniform in Z_q^{M(d)×d}, and let the coordinates of e be independent integers with probability proportional to exp(−πz²/(4d)), reduced modulo q. The ensembles (A,As+e mod q) and (A,u), for independent uniform u∈Z_q^{M(d)}, are computationally indistinguishable against nonuniform classical circuits of size polynomial in d. Thus the error distribution is the discrete Gaussian D_{Z,2√d}; only ordinary independently generated LWE samples are assumed hard. The FHE scheme has uniform classical polynomial-time algorithms Gen(1^λ)→(pk,evk,sk), Enc(pk,b), Eval(evk,C,c₁,…,c_t), and Dec(sk,c), with bit plaintexts and Boolean circuits over AND, OR and NOT. Gen takes no circuit-size or depth bound. There is one fixed polynomial P such that keys, fresh bit ciphertexts, evaluated one-bit ciphertexts and the time to decrypt a valid output are bounded by P(λ), independently of C and t. Evaluation is polynomial-time in λ and its total input length. For every polynomial p, uniformly over all circuits C of size and input count at most p(λ) and all input bits b₁,…,b_t, decrypting Eval on independent encryptions of these bits equals C(b₁,…,b_t), except with negligible probability over generation, encryption and evaluation. Ordinary decryption is correct with negligible error. Given both pk and evk, every nonuniform polynomial-size classical adversary has negligible advantage in distinguishing an encryption of 0 from one of 1. Negligible means smaller than λ^{-a} eventually for every a>0. No subsequent secret-key assistance, ideal oracle, external trusted setup, superpolynomial adversary-hardness assumption, functional-encryption assumption or obfuscation assumption is allowed. This fixes a polynomial-modulus version of “standard LWE”; it does not assume any encryptions of secrets or correlated hints are secure.

cards.title: Smaller shares for general secret sharing
cards.formal: Do there exist real constants K>0 and 0<c<1/2 such that, for every n≥1 and every monotone access structure Γ on [n] with ∅∉Γ and [n]∈Γ, there exists a perfect secret-sharing scheme for a uniform one-bit secret with max_i log₂|S_i|≤K·2^(cn), where S_i is the finite alphabet of participant i’s share?
cards.definitions: [n]={1,…,n}. An access structure Γ⊆2^[n] is monotone when A∈Γ and A⊆B⊆[n] imply B∈Γ. A scheme is a joint probability distribution of a secret B uniform on {0,1} and shares X_i∈S_i, where each S_i is a finite nonempty set. For each A∈Γ there is a deterministic map r_A:∏_{i∈A}S_i→{0,1} such that r_A((X_i)_{i∈A})=B with probability one. For each A∉Γ, the conditional distributions of (X_i)_{i∈A} given B=0 and B=1 are identical. This is exact reconstruction and perfect information-theoretic privacy, with arbitrary collusion within A. Share size is the base-two logarithm of its alphabet cardinality, not its Shannon entropy or the sum over participants. It is normalized by the secret size of one bit. There is no linearity, field, threshold, computation-time or uniform construction requirement. The scheme may depend on the whole finite access structure. K,c must be universal. Rounding log₂|S_i| up to an integer encoding length changes K only by an absolute factor.

cards.title: Quantum PCP: a constant promise gap for local Hamiltonians
cards.formal: Do there exist integers k,d≥1 and a rational constant ε∈(0,1) such that the following promise problem is QMA-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions? Input is a list of m≤(n+1)^d k-local Hermitian terms H_i on n≥1 qubits and rational a<b in [0,1], with 0⪯H_i⪯I and b−a≥ε. For H=(1/m)Σ_i H_i, distinguish λ_min(H)≤a from λ_min(H)≥b.
cards.definitions: Here 1≤m; each term is specified by at most k distinct qubit indices and the complete matrix on those qubits, with rational real and imaginary parts encoded by signed binary numerators and positive denominators. It is tensored with identity on the other qubits. n is written in unary, thresholds in binary rational notation; N counts every supplied bit. λ_min is the smallest eigenvalue. M⪯N means that N−M is positive semidefinite, equivalently z*(N−M)z≥0 for every complex vector z. Inputs violating the matrix promises or with a<λ_min(H)<b are outside the promise. QMA consists of disjoint pairs (Y,N₀) of sets of binary strings with a polynomial-time uniform quantum verifier: on x it uses polynomially many qubits and gates over {H,T,CNOT}, an arbitrary polynomial-qubit witness, and auxiliary qubits initialized to |0⟩. H=2^(−1/2)((1,1),(1,−1)) is the Hadamard matrix, T=diag(1,exp(iπ/4)), and CNOT flips its target when its control is 1. A designated final qubit is measured. For x∈Y some witness gives acceptance probability ≥2/3; for x∈N₀ every witness gives probability ≤1/3. A deterministic machine produces the verifier circuit from x in polynomial time. QMA-hard means that for every such pair there is a deterministic polynomial-time map sending Y into the low-energy case and N₀ into the high-energy case, always producing legal instances on promised inputs. Constants k,d,ε are shared by the target problem; reduction polynomials may depend on the source promise problem.

cards.title: Does BPP differ from BQP?

Size and register bounds use fixed polynomial exponents independent of n. Equivalent standard uniform quantum-machine definitions give the same class. The problem concerns one-bit decisions on all binary strings, with no promise on the input. cards.title: An entanglement entropy area law for general gapped two-dimensional Hamiltonians
cards.formal: For every fixed local dimension q≥2, interaction range r≥1, interaction incidence bound g≥1, norm bound J>0, and spectral gap Δ>0, is there a finite constant C=C(q,r,g,J,Δ) such that every Hamiltonian H described below, on every square lattice Λ_L, has unique ground state ψ satisfying S(ρ_A)≤C|∂A| for every A⊆Λ_L?
cards.definitions: Let L≥1 be an integer, Λ_L={1,…,L}² with open boundaries, and the Hilbert space be the tensor product of C^q over its sites. Write H=Σ_a h_a, where each h_a is Hermitian and acts only on a nonempty support X_a⊆Λ_L of diameter at most r in the maximum-coordinate metric. Each site belongs to at most g supports, counting terms with the same support separately, and the operator norm of every h_a is at most J. Suppose H has a unique normalized lowest-energy eigenvector ψ and its next eigenvalue is at least Δ above the lowest eigenvalue. This is a gap of the entire Hamiltonian; no spectral-gap condition is imposed on subregions or subsets of terms. For A⊆Λ_L, let A^c be its complement in Λ_L and ρ_A=Tr_(A^c)(|ψ⟩⟨ψ|) and S(ρ_A)=−Tr(ρ_A log_2 ρ_A), with 0 log_2 0=0. The boundary ∂A is the set of nearest-neighbor lattice edges with exactly one endpoint in A; its cardinality is the boundary length in lattice units. Empty and full regions have entropy zero. The local parameters and C must be independent of L, A, and the actual interaction matrices. Interactions may vary from site to site and with L. They need not commute or share a simultaneous minimum-energy state; translation invariance and frustration freeness are not assumed. No approximation or state-preparation algorithm is requested.

cards.formal: Do there exist finite integers a,b≥2 and a bipartite density matrix ρ on ℂᵃ⊗ℂᵇ such that ρ has negative partial transpose, but ⟨ψ|(ρ^{Γ_B})^{⊗k}|ψ⟩≥0 for every integer k≥1 and every unit vector ψ of Schmidt rank at most two across (ℂᵃ)^{⊗k}:(ℂᵇ)^{⊗k}?
cards.definitions: A density matrix is a positive semidefinite Hermitian matrix with trace one. In fixed local orthonormal bases, partial transpose on B is defined by (ρ^{Γ_B})_{ij,kℓ}=ρ_{iℓ,kj}. Negative partial transpose (NPT) means that ρ^{Γ_B} has at least one negative eigenvalue; it does not mean that the whole matrix is negative semidefinite. Schmidt rank is the minimum number of product vectors whose sum is ψ. Tensor powers represent independent copies of the same fixed state. A state is k-copy distillable exactly when a Schmidt-rank-at-most-two vector makes the displayed expectation strictly negative. Thus the proposed state is undistillable for every finite number of copies. Operationally, Alice and Bob may use arbitrary local quantum operations, local auxiliary systems and unlimited classical communication in both directions, but no quantum communication or additional shared entanglement. Distillability means that they can asymptotically obtain Bell pairs (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2 at a positive rate with error tending to zero. The finite-copy criterion above is equivalent to positive distillability in this model.

cards.title: Martin’s full conjecture for Turing-invariant functions under determinacy
cards.formal: Assume ZF+DC+AD. Do both assertions hold? (I) Every Turing-invariant function f:2^ω→2^ω is either constant in Turing degree on a cone or satisfies x≤_T f(x) on a cone. (II) Cone-wise Turing reducibility prewellorders all such functions that are above the identity on a cone, and the pointwise jump f′ has rank exactly rank(f)+1 in this prewellorder.
cards.definitions: A real x∈2^ω is an infinite binary sequence, identified with a subset of the natural numbers. Write x≤_T y if an oracle Turing machine with oracle y computes x, and x≡_T y for mutual reducibility. A function f is Turing-invariant when x≡_T y implies f(x)≡_T f(y). A cone above a real a is {x:a≤_T x}. Being constant on a cone means ∃a,b ∀x≥_T a, f(x)≡_T b; the output sequences need not be literally equal. Define f≤_M g by ∃a ∀x≥_T a, f(x)≤_T g(x), and f≡_M g by mutual ≤_M. Let F be the set of all Turing-invariant f for which id≤_M f, where id(x)=x. The prewellorder assertion says that ≤_M is total on F and its quotient by ≡_M is well-ordered. The rank of f is the ordinal order type of the quotient classes strictly preceding [f]. The jump of a real y is y′={e: the e-th oracle program with oracle y halts on input e}; f′(x)=f(x)′. ZF is Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory without the axiom of choice. DC is dependent choice: every serial binary relation on a nonempty set admits an infinite successive chain. AD says every infinite game in which two players alternately choose natural numbers, with an arbitrary specified set of winning sequences, is determined. Functions are not assumed computable, Borel, order-preserving, or uniformly Turing-invariant. Cone bases may depend on the functions being compared.

cards.title: Kolmogorov–Loveland randomness versus Martin-Löf randomness
cards.formal: Is every Kolmogorov–Loveland random infinite binary sequence Martin-Löf random with respect to the fair-coin product measure?
cards.definitions: Work in Cantor space 2^N, with coordinates numbered 0,1,… and fair-coin product measure μ. For a finite binary string σ, the cylinder [σ]={X:σ is a prefix of X} has measure 2^{−|σ|}. A Martin-Löf test is a sequence (U_k)_{k≥1} of open sets obtained by one algorithm enumerating pairs (k,σ), with U_k equal to the union of its enumerated cylinders for index k and μ(U_k)≤2^{−k}. A sequence X is Martin-Löf random if for every such test X∉⋂_k U_k. A Kolmogorov–Loveland betting strategy starts with capital 1. From the finite history h of bits already revealed, a partial computable procedure outputs a previously unqueried coordinate j and a rational multiplier q∈[0,2], before seeing X(j). The selected coordinates can be reconstructed from the earlier history and the same procedure; no coordinate may be selected twice along any run. After X(j) is revealed, the capital is multiplied by q if the bit is 0 and by 2−q if it is 1, and that bit is appended to h. Thus each bet preserves expected capital under a fresh unbiased bit and cannot create debt. q=1 allows reading a bit without risking capital. The next coordinate may depend on all revealed values and need not exceed previous coordinates. If the procedure fails to produce its next action, no further capital is earned. There are no oracle, running-time or space allowances beyond ordinary partial computability. A strategy succeeds on X if its capital at completed bets has unbounded supremum. X is Kolmogorov–Loveland random if every such strategy has bounded capital on X; the bound may depend on both X and the strategy. Rational multipliers suffice for the standard notion, and allowing partial rather than total computable strategies does not change the resulting class.

cards.title: Do some tautologies require superpolynomial Extended Frege proofs?
cards.formal: Is Extended Frege not polynomially bounded? Precisely, for every constants C>0 and c≥1, is there a propositional tautology φ whose shortest Extended Frege proof has bit length greater than C(|φ|+2)ᶜ? Here |φ| is the bit length of the explicitly written formula.
cards.definitions: Fix Boolean formulas over ¬ and →, with → interpreted as material implication and variable indices encoded in binary. Use the Frege axiom schemes A→(B→A), (A→(B→C))→((A→B)→(A→C)), and (¬B→¬A)→(A→B), together with modus ponens from A and A→B to B. An Extended Frege proof of φ may additionally introduce an abbreviation variable e by the two extension axioms e→θ and θ→e. Here e is fresh, absent from φ, θ, and every preceding line; θ uses original variables of φ and previously introduced extension variables. Extensions are thus acyclic definitions. Other proof lines are axiom instances or applications of modus ponens, and the last line must be φ, with no extension variables. Lines may cite and reuse earlier lines arbitrarily: proofs are not required to be trees. Proof size is the full binary encoding length of all explicitly written formulas, extension definitions, and inference references; there is no depth or per-line-size restriction. A tautology is true under every assignment to its variables. This fixed presentation is polynomially equivalent to the usual Extended Frege systems, so changing a standard finite Frege basis does not change polynomial boundedness. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.

cards.title: Can randomness always be removed from polynomial-time decision algorithms?
cards.formal: Does P=BPP? Precisely, for every language L for which a randomized Turing machine R runs in polynomial time on every input and every random tape, and satisfies $\Pr[R(x)=1_L(x)]\ge2/3$ for every binary string x, does there exist a deterministic polynomial-time Turing machine deciding L correctly on every x? The polynomial time bound of the deterministic machine may depend on R.
cards.definitions: Input length is n=|x|. A polynomial-time bound means C(n+1)^k steps for fixed constants C,k, independent of x and of the random bits. R uses independent unbiased random bits, at most one fresh bit per computation step, and outputs a single bit. Its error may be on either yes or no inputs, but is bounded separately on each input. P consists of deterministic polynomial-time decision languages and BPP of languages meeting the randomized guarantee above. These are total decision problems, with no excluded promise inputs. No advice, oracle, quantum operations, or input distribution is allowed. The requested deterministic simulation may use a different algorithm; it need not reproduce R's random choices, preserve its precise exponent, or be generated by an effective compiler from R.

cards.title: Optimal explicit pseudorandom generators for read-once branching programs
cards.formal: Do there exist absolute constants C,D and a uniform family of generators G_{n,w,p}:{0,1}^s→{0,1}^n, for all integers n,w≥2 and p≥1, with s≤C(log_2 n+log_2 w+p), such that |Pr_{u uniform in {0,1}^s}[B(G_{n,w,p}(u))=1]−Pr_{z uniform in {0,1}^n}[B(z)=1]|≤2^(−p) for every length-n, width-at-most-w ordered read-once branching program B? Require a single deterministic algorithm that, given n,w,p,u and an output position i, computes G_{n,w,p}(u)_i using at most D(log_2 n+log_2 w+p) work bits and time (nw·2^p)^D.
cards.definitions: An ordered read-once branching program has layers V_0,…,V_n, each containing at most w states, a designated initial state in V_0, and an accepting subset of V_n. For each layer i−1, each state has one outgoing edge labeled 0 and one labeled 1 to V_i. On input z, the program follows the edge labeled z_i at step i and accepts exactly when the final state is accepting. Different edges may merge; neither regularity nor permutation transitions are required. The order is the fixed order z_1,…,z_n. Programs may be arbitrary nonuniform objects, but the generator cannot inspect their descriptions. The parameters and seed are read-only inputs to the generator algorithm, and the output bit is written separately; all work space, counters and intermediate storage are counted. Seed length is a computable function of the parameters within the stated resources. Uniform seeds induce an ordinary probability distribution, without signed or externally assigned weights. Set ε=2^(−p); this dyadic formulation gives the usual O(log(nw/ε)) target for arbitrary positive error by rounding down to a smaller dyadic tolerance.
