cards.title: Is k-Clique fixed-parameter tractable, equivalently FPT=W[1]?
cards.formal: Do there exist a total computable function f:ℕ→ℕ, a constant c, and one deterministic algorithm that decides whether an n-vertex graph contains a k-clique in time at most f(k)(n+2)ᶜ on every input? Equivalently, is FPT=W[1]?
cards.definitions: An instance is a finite simple undirected graph G on [n], encoded by its adjacency matrix, and an integer k with 0≤k≤n, encoded in binary. A k-clique is a set of k distinct vertices for which every pair is an edge; k=0 is a yes-instance. Inputs with k>n are rejected immediately, and other malformed inputs are rejected. The parameter is k, not treewidth, degree, or the size of a supplied decomposition. Running time counts deterministic Turing-machine steps on the full input. Constants and the function f may be arbitrary but must be fixed independently of n; the exponent c must also be independent of k. FPT comprises parameterized decision problems solvable in f(k)Nᶜ time, where N is their input encoding length. One equivalent definition of W[1] is the class of parameterized problems reducible to k-Clique by a deterministic f(k)Nᶜ-time many-one reduction whose output parameter is bounded by a computable function of k alone. This is the standard parameterized reduction convention under which Clique is W[1]-complete. No randomness, advice, or promise about G is allowed.

cards.title: Does deterministic 3-SAT have a positive optimal exponential rate?
cards.formal: Is there a constant c>0 such that, for every deterministic algorithm A that correctly decides every 3-CNF satisfiability instance, and every constant d≥0, A does not have worst-case running time O(2^{cn}L^d)? Here n is the number of variables and L is the full binary input length. This is the deterministic Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH).
cards.definitions: A 3-CNF formula is a conjunction of explicitly listed clauses, each containing at most three literals xᵢ or ¬xᵢ. Satisfiability means existence of a Boolean assignment satisfying all clauses. Variables are relabeled consecutively; n counts the distinct variables actually present, and L includes all literal indices, signs, delimiters, and repetitions. An empty clause is unsatisfiable and an empty conjunction is satisfiable. Algorithms are uniform deterministic Turing machines with no advice or oracles; they must halt and answer exactly on all inputs, with no promise about density, solution count, or distribution. Define s₃=inf{α≥0 : some such algorithm runs in O(2^{αn}L^d) for a fixed d}. ETH asserts s₃>0. The excluded exponent c is a single constant independent of the algorithm. The polynomial exponent and hidden constant may depend on the algorithm, but not the instance. Polynomial input factors allow the complete formula to be read even if clauses are repeated many times. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.

cards.title: Constant-factor approximation for Densest k-Subgraph
cards.area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
cards.formal: Do there exist a universal constant C≥1 and a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm A such that, for every finite simple undirected unweighted graph G=(V,E) and every integer 1≤k≤|V|, A(G,k) outputs a set S⊆V with |S|=k and |E(G[S])|≥OPT(G,k)/C, where OPT(G,k)=max_{T⊆V, |T|=k}|E(G[T])|?
cards.definitions: G is explicitly represented by its vertices and edges, and k is supplied in binary as part of the input. G[S] contains all edges of G with both endpoints in S; loops and parallel edges are absent. The running time is polynomial in the full input length with a fixed exponent independent of k. The same finite C must work for all graphs, all graph sizes and all choices of k; it cannot increase with n=|V| or with k. The output must be a vertex set, not only an estimate of the optimum. When OPT=0, every k-set meets the requirement. Because all feasible sets have the same cardinality, maximizing edge count, average degree 2|E(G[S])|/k, or edges per selected vertex gives the same approximation objective. This card fixes deterministic algorithms; a randomized constant-factor guarantee would be major progress but has a distinct derandomization requirement. cards.title: The deterministic k-server conjecture
cards.formal: For every integer k≥1, every metric space (M,d) with at least k+1 points, and every initial placement C_0 of k servers, does there exist a deterministic online serving rule A and a finite constant β≥0 such that cost_A(σ;C_0)≤k·OPT(σ;C_0)+β for every finite request sequence σ∈M*? The rule and β may depend on M,d,k,C_0, but neither may depend on future requests or on the length of the request sequence.
cards.definitions: The metric is symmetric, has finite real distances, is zero exactly on equal points, and satisfies the triangle inequality; the space may be finite or infinite and is known to the online rule. There are exactly k interchangeable, unweighted servers, whose current positions form a multiset. A request r_t must be served before r_{t+1} is revealed. If a server is already at r_t, no movement is needed; otherwise the rule chooses one of the k servers and moves it to r_t, paying the metric distance. Restriction to these lazy moves loses no competitive power. A deterministic online rule is a function of the known metric, initial placement and revealed request prefix, with arbitrary memory and no access to future requests; this card imposes no running-time bound. OPT is the minimum total movement cost of an offline rule serving the same finite sequence from C_0 with the same k servers and advance knowledge of the sequence. The additive β must be fixed before requests arrive and cannot grow with the number or cost of requests. Randomization, advice about future requests, and extra servers are not supplied.

cards.title: Does P≠NP imply a samplable NP problem outside AvgP?
cards.formal: Is the implication $\mathrm{P}\ne\mathrm{NP}\Longrightarrow(\mathrm{NP},\mathrm{PSamp})\nsubseteq\mathrm{AvgP}$ true? That is, assuming P≠NP, must there exist a language L∈NP and a polynomial-time samplable distribution ensemble D={Dₙ} such that no deterministic exact decider for L runs in average polynomial time under D, in the moment-based sense defined below?
cards.definitions: A sampler is one randomized Turing machine S which, given 1ⁿ, halts within q(n) steps on every random tape for a fixed polynomial q. Its output distribution Dₙ is over finite binary strings x; |x|≤q(n), and n is the ensemble parameter, not necessarily |x|. Sampling is exact with independent unbiased coin flips, and S has no advice or oracle. An exact decider A receives (1ⁿ,x), halts, and returns the membership bit of L correctly for every n and x. Write T_A(1ⁿ,x) for its running time. The pair (L,D) belongs to AvgP if there exist such an A, ε>0, C>0, and integer k≥1 with $\mathbb E_{x\sim D_n}[T_A(1^n,x)^\varepsilon]\le C(n+1)^k$ for every n≥1. The constants and A may depend on L and S but not on n. This moment definition is the robust Levin notion, not the requirement that the first moment itself be polynomial. The algorithm is deterministic and never gives a wrong answer; difficult inputs may take a long time. NP uses ordinary polynomially bounded certificates and deterministic polynomial-time verification. Both the hard language and its sampler must be fixed across all input lengths.

cards.title: Constant-factor universally truthful auctions for submodular bidders
cards.area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
cards.formal: Does there exist a universal constant C≥1 and a randomized, universally truthful combinatorial-auction mechanism that, for every number n of bidders, number m of items and normalized monotone submodular valuation profile, uses polynomial communication and produces an allocation of expected social welfare at least OPT/C?

Bidder i privately knows v_i:2^[m]→Q_{≥0}, with v_i(∅)=0, v_i(S)≤v_i(T) for S⊆T, and v_i(S)+v_i(T)≥v_i(S∪T)+v_i(S∩T) for all S,T. To make communication in bits precise, a public integer B≥1 bounds the binary lengths of the numerator and positive denominator of each value. This is a bound per value, not permission to transmit the exponential table. One uniform protocol must work for every n,m,B with at most P(n,m,B) communicated bits in the worst case, for one fixed polynomial P. Arbitrary interactive messages and demand queries are allowed; all query descriptions, replies, allocations and payments count toward communication. Local computation by bidders and auctioneer is unrestricted but must terminate. An outcome consists of pairwise disjoint bundles S_1,…,S_n and rational payments p_1,…,p_n; unallocated items are allowed. Utilities are quasilinear, u_i=v_i(S_i)−p_i. There are no private budgets or distributional assumptions. Universal truthfulness means the mechanism is a report-independent distribution over deterministic dominant-strategy truthful mechanisms: for every fixed random seed r, every i, every admissible true and alternative reported type v_i,v_i′, and every v_{−i}, v_i(S_i(v_i,v_{−i};r))−p_i(v_i,v_{−i};r)≥v_i(S_i(v_i′,v_{−i};r))−p_i(v_i′,v_{−i};r). cards.title: The exact capacity region of the two-user Gaussian interference channel
cards.formal: Determine the capacity region C(a,b,P₁,P₂) of the memoryless real channel Y₁,t=X₁,t+aX₂,t+Z₁,t and Y₂,t=bX₁,t+X₂,t+Z₂,t for every fixed a,b∈ℝ and finite P₁,P₂≥0, with independent messages, average power constraints, no feedback or cooperation, and vanishing average decoding error. Equivalently, determine the exact function F(a,b,P₁,P₂,λ)=sup_{(R₁,R₂)∈C}[λR₁+(1−λ)R₂] for every λ∈[0,1], under the operational definitions below.
cards.definitions: For a block of n uses, messages M_i are independent and uniform on {1,…,K_{i,n}}. Transmitter i applies a deterministic encoder f_{i,n}:{1,…,K_{i,n}}→ℝⁿ depending only on its own message. Its codebook satisfies (nK_{i,n})⁻¹∑_{m=1}^{K_{i,n}}∑_{t=1}ⁿ f_{i,n}(m)_t²≤P_i. All Z_{i,t} are mutually independent N(0,1) random variables independent of the messages. Receiver i applies a measurable decoder g_{i,n}:ℝⁿ→{1,…,K_{i,n}} to its own received vector. The probability that either decoded message is wrong is averaged over both messages and all noise. A nonnegative pair (R₁,R₂) is achievable if there is a sequence of such codes with this error tending to zero and liminf_{n→∞} n⁻¹ log₂ K_{i,n}≥R_i for i=1,2. C is the closure of achievable pairs, measured in bits per real channel use. Gains, powers and both codebooks are known to all terminals. Arbitrary encoding across time and predetermined time sharing with power allocation are permitted; transmitters have no messages in common, output feedback, or communication between them. C is compact, convex and downward closed, so the nonnegative supporting function F uniquely determines it.

cards.title: Effective classification of polynomially testable hereditary graph properties
cards.formal: Is there a total algorithm which, given a finite family F of finite simple graphs, decides whether induced-F-freeness admits a one-sided dense-model tester sampling at most C·ε^{−c} vertices, for some constants C,c depending only on F?
cards.definitions: The input to the classification algorithm is a finite list of adjacency matrices; the empty list is allowed. Let P_F contain exactly the finite simple graphs with no induced subgraph isomorphic to any member of F. For an n-vertex graph G, define dist(G,P_F) as the minimum number of edge additions or deletions needed to obtain a graph in P_F on the same vertex set, divided by n²; define the distance as +∞ when no such graph exists. For an integer s, the canonical tester chooses a uniformly random subset S of min{n,s} distinct vertices, queries all adjacencies in S, and rejects exactly when G[S] contains an induced member of F. Say that F is polynomially testable if there are integers C,c≥1 such that for every rational ε∈(0,1), every n≥1 and every G with dist(G,P_F)>ε, this tester with s=⌈Cε^{−c}⌉ rejects with probability at least 2/3. It automatically accepts every graph in P_F. The requested deterministic classification algorithm must halt on every finite F and answer YES exactly for these families. No runtime bound on that classification algorithm is imposed, and it need not output the constants C,c. Graph order n and accuracy ε are universally quantified in the property being classified; they are not additional inputs to the classification algorithm.

cards.title: Does polynomial testability imply polynomial distance estimation for dense graph properties?
cards.formal: For every isomorphism-invariant property P of finite simple graphs with P_n nonempty for every n≥1, does existence of a uniform randomized tester using polynomially many queries in 1/ε, independently of n, imply existence of such an additive-ε distance estimator, in the dense model defined below?

An algorithm receives n and an integer t≥2, with ε=1/t, and accesses G only by adaptive queries asking whether a specified unordered pair is an edge. A tester returns a bit, accepts each G∈P_n with probability ≥2/3 and rejects each G with dist(G,P)≥ε with probability ≥2/3; no condition is imposed between those cases. Polynomial testability means there exist one probabilistic Turing oracle machine and constants C,a≥1 with at most Ct^a adjacency queries on every input and every execution. Computation between queries and total output length have no prescribed bound, but every execution terminates. Coins are independent fair bits; programs and constants may depend on P and cannot depend on n,t or G. Neither algorithm receives a description of P or graph-dependent advice. This asks only the polynomial-testability implication named in the title. The stronger quantitative q_P(poly(ε)) conversion in source Problem 5.4 is not asserted equivalent to it.

cards.title: Is private PAC sample complexity polynomial in VC dimension and log-star Littlestone dimension?
cards.formal: Is there a universal polynomial p such that every nonempty finite Boolean concept class C on a finite nonempty domain X admits a realizable, possibly improper PAC learner using some number $m\le p(1+\mathrm{VC}(C),1+\log^*\mathrm{LD}(C))$ of independent labeled examples, with error at most 1/10 and confidence at least 9/10, while satisfying $(1,1/(100m^2))$-differential privacy? The learning guarantee must hold for every distribution on the domain and every target concept in C. Computation time is unrestricted. Take both dimensions to be at least one; constant classes can be handled separately.
cards.definitions: A concept class is a finite set of functions from a domain X to {0,1}. VC(C) is the largest size of a subset of X on which all binary labelings occur. LD(C) is the greatest depth of a complete binary tree labeled by domain points such that every root-to-leaf edge-label sequence is realized by a concept. The function log-star counts base-two logarithms needed to reach at most one. A learner may output a hypothesis outside C. Privacy requires $\Pr[A(S)\in E]\le e\Pr[A(S\prime)\in E]+1/(100m^2)$ whenever the two m-record samples differ by replacement of one record. Here X is finite, distributions on X are arbitrary probability vectors, and a learner is a probability kernel from length-m labeled samples to the finite set {0,1}^X of hypotheses. The sample size m is a positive integer chosen for C before the target and distribution. For every target h∈C and distribution D on X, with probability at least 9/10 over m independent draws x_i from D and learner randomness, the returned hypothesis has D-probability of disagreement with h at most 1/10. Privacy holds for all labeled samples, including unrealizable ones, and all subsets E of the hypothesis set. The same kernel and m work for all D,h. This finite-domain convention retains the finite-class target: points in an arbitrary domain with the same label vector (h(x))_{h∈C} can be identified, giving at most 2^|C| cells and preserving both dimensions. A learner on those cells lifts to the original domain. No running-time or computable-representation requirement is imposed.

cards.title: Does every finite-template decision promise CSP have a P/NP-hard dichotomy?
cards.formal: For every pair of fixed finite relational structures A,B of the same finite signature, with a homomorphism A→B, is the decision promise problem of distinguishing I→A from I↛B either solvable in deterministic polynomial time or NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one promise reductions?
cards.definitions: A finite relational signature is a finite list of relation symbols R with fixed positive arities a_R. A structure A consists of a finite nonempty domain and, for each R, a relation R^A⊆A^{a_R}. A homomorphism h:I→A is a map on domains such that (v₁,…,v_a)∈R^I implies (h(v₁),…,h(v_a))∈R^A for every R and tuple. The templates A,B and their relations are fixed for each computational problem. Only I varies; its domain and relation tuples are explicitly listed in binary, of total length L. The algorithm must accept all I admitting a homomorphism to A and reject all I admitting no homomorphism to B. On I→B but I↛A, either answer is allowed. A→B makes the yes and no sets disjoint. Polynomial time means one deterministic algorithm for the fixed pair, halting on every input in O(L^c), with c and hidden constants allowed to depend on A,B. NP-hardness means a deterministic polynomial-time map from 3-SAT formulas φ to structures I_φ such that satisfiable φ yield I_φ→A and unsatisfiable φ yield I_φ↛B. The question is about deciding the promise, not producing a B-valued assignment. No uniform algorithm for classifying templates is required. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.

cards.formal: For every countable finitely bounded homogeneous structure A over a finite relational signature, and every finite-signature first-order reduct B of A, is CSP(B) either decidable in deterministic polynomial time or NP-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions?
cards.definitions: A relational signature is a finite list of relation symbols with fixed finite arities. A is homogeneous if every isomorphism between two finite induced substructures extends to an automorphism of A. It is finitely bounded if there is a finite set F of finite structures in its signature such that a finite structure embeds into A exactly when none of the structures in F embeds into it; embeddings preserve both relations and their complements. B has the same domain as A, with finitely many relations each definable by a first-order formula over A without parameters; it may forget original relations and introduce definable ones. Accept exactly when there is a map h from the domain of I to that of B preserving every relation tuple. Equivalently, a finite conjunction of atomic B-constraints must have a satisfying assignment. h need not be injective. A, B and their defining formulas are fixed, not part of the input; running times are measured in the finite instance’s bit length. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.

cards.formal: Is there a deterministic Turing machine that halts on every finite modal formula φ and decides whether there exists a substitution σ for its propositional variables such that σ(φ) is valid on every Kripke frame?

cards.title: FO model checking on hereditary monadically dependent graph classes
cards.area: Database theory and finite model theory
cards.formal: For every hereditary effectively monadically dependent class C of finite simple graphs, do there exist a deterministic algorithm A_C, a computable function f_C:N→N and a constant d_C such that A_C decides whether G satisfies a first-order sentence φ in time f_C(|φ|)(|V(G)|+1)^{d_C} for every G∈C? The precise effectiveness condition is given below; the graph is supplied without a structural decomposition.
cards.definitions: The class C is fixed, is closed under isomorphism and induced subgraphs, and is not part of each input. First-order sentences use equality, adjacency E(x,y), Boolean connectives and quantifiers over individual vertices. They do not quantify over sets, and no vertex order or arithmetic is supplied. The input is the explicitly represented graph G and the sentence φ; the parameter k=|φ| is its encoded length. The algorithm must halt on every input, and its correctness and stated time bound are required when G∈C; it need not recognize membership in C. To define monadic dependence, let θ(x,y) be any fixed first-order formula using adjacency and finitely many additional unary predicates. A graph in T_θ(G) is obtained by interpreting these predicates as arbitrary vertex subsets, putting an edge between distinct u,v whenever θ(u,v) or θ(v,u) holds, and taking any induced subgraph. C is monadically dependent when no single θ gives all finite graphs among the outputs T_θ(G), G∈C. For an explicit effective version, define P_s as the bipartite powerset graph with vertices a₁,…,a_s and b_S for every S⊆{1,…,s}, and edges a_i b_S exactly when i∈S. Require a computable function b:N→N_{≥1} such that, for every formula θ and every G∈C, P_{b(|θ|)} is absent from T_θ(G). Formula length includes its predicate symbols under a fixed effective encoding. This is the computable dependence-function convention of Mählmann’s Definition 12.24. The programs computing b and the eventual algorithm may depend on C; they are not extra per-instance certificates. The exponent d_C is independent of k. The query-evaluation problem here is for the plain graph signature; unary colours occur in the structural definition. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.

cards.title: The full constant-delay conjunctive-query classification
cards.area: Database theory and finite model theory
cards.formal: Is there a total algorithm that, given any conjunctive query q with self-joins allowed, decides whether q admits enumeration of all distinct answers with O_q(N) preprocessing and O_q(1) worst-case delay on every database of size N?
cards.definitions: A query is a finite formula q(x̄)=∃ȳ ∧ᵢ Rᵢ(z̄ᵢ), with no constants, negation, disequalities or aggregation. The head x̄ lists distinct variables; every variable occurs in a relational atom. Relation symbols have fixed positive finite arities within q and may occur repeatedly; repeated variables within atoms are allowed. Boolean queries have an empty head. A database D explicitly lists finite set-valued relations over a domain [n]; N=1+n+the total number of tuple entries in these lists. Each domain identifier fits in O(log(N+2)) bits. q(D) is the set of head tuples extendible to an assignment satisfying all atoms. Fix the deterministic word-RAM convention with addition, multiplication, comparison, Boolean word operations and indirect access costing one step, words of O_q(log(N+2)) bits, and a polynomial address universe of initially zero cells. Accessed cells and operations are charged; no linear-space or constant-extra-space restriction is imposed. This allows direct tuple-membership tables without charging for touching every unused address. Membership in the target class means that for this fixed q there are an enumerator and constants C_q,B_q whose preprocessing takes at most C_q N steps, whose word length is at most B_q log₂(N+2), and whose time to the first answer, between consecutive answers, and from the last answer to termination is at most C_q after preprocessing. Empty output must be reported within the same delay bound. Output order is arbitrary and each tuple appears exactly once. The classifier takes q, not D, as input and must halt on every query; it has no prescribed runtime bound and need not output the enumerator. This is an explicit effective yes/no formulation of the source’s broader request for a complete tractability classification. The word instructions are random-access reads/writes, comparisons, conditional branches, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo 2^w, integer quotient/remainder with nonzero divisor, bitwise Boolean operations, and shifts of a w-bit word; shifts by at least w yield zero. The constant in word length w=Θ(log n) (or Θ(log N) when N is the stated input size) is fixed with the algorithm. Address arithmetic has the same cost, larger integers occupy multiple words, and no instruction performs arbitrary-precision arithmetic in one step. When randomization is allowed, a fresh independent uniform w-bit word costs one operation. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.
